title: By the Poor Widow's Oil and Meal
description: By the Poor Widow's Oil and Meal in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 36, “The meal and Cruse of oil. 1Ki 17:16”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: By the poor wid-ow's oil and meal E-li-jah was sus-tained; Though small the stock it last-ed well, For God the store main-tained.

lines: By the poor widow's oil and meal
Elijah was sustained;
Though small the stock it lasted well,
For God the store maintained.
It seemed as if from day to day,
They were to eat and die;
But still, though in a secret way,
He sent a fresh supply.
Thus to his poor he still will give
Just for the present hour;
But for tomorrow they must live
Upon his word and power.
No barn or storehouse they possess
On which they can depend;
Yet have no cause to fear distress,
For Jesus is their friend.
Then let not doubts your mind assail,
Remember, God has said,
"The cruse and barrel shall not fail,
"My people shall be fed."
And thus though faint it often seems,
He keeps their grace alive;
Supplied by his refreshing streams,
Their dying hopes revive.
Though in ourselves we have no stock,
The Lord is nigh to save;
His door flies open when we knock,
And 'tis but ask and have.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
